messages:
mira_support: FYI incoming customer escalation from Acme Ops — their indexing pipeline started failing during nightly ingest, lots of errors referencing dimension mismatch and intermittent 429s from the embeddings endpoint. They say this started after a model swap we suggested last week. Ticket #C-5492.

acme_ops: seeing ~30% of batches rejected. Error in our indexer: 'expected vector dim=1536, got=1024' for some ids, while others ingest fine. Also seeing `HTTP 429` when we push >8 docs/s to /embeddings.

mira_support: can you paste the exact embed response and indexer error? Also confirm which model they were using before/after?

acme_ops: before: `open-embed-1536-v1` (hosted by us), after: `open-embed-1024-q4` (we asked to try a cheaper quantized variant). Responses:
```json
{
  "model": "open-embed-1024-q4",
  "embedding": [0.003, -0.12, ...],
  "length": 1024
}
```
Index error log (snippet):
```
IndexerError: VectorDimMismatch: id=acme-usr-123 expected=1536 got=1024 at indexer/worker.py:412
  File "indexer/worker.py", line 412, in add_batch
    raise VectorDimMismatch(req_id)
```

alex_eng: ok that explains the dim mismatch. The surprising part is the partial success — implies some embeddings are still 1536. Two hypotheses: 1) mixed model usage (some requests hitting old model), 2) post-processing step in pipeline reusing cached embeddings.

jordan_sre: I pulled the request logs from the edge for Acme's account during the window (03:00-03:20 UTC). Found a token rotation event at 03:05 where the auth token TTL renewed and a little spike in 429s from our hosted embed pool around the same time. Rate limiter logs show Acme had a brief burst at 03:06 that exceeded their per-minute quota -> produced 429 from embeddings service.

ying_ml: important detail — the new model `open-embed-1024-q4` was deployed as a variant under the same model name in their config, and we didn't migrate the indexing schema. When you swap the model we should warn customers to re-run their ingest or set a migration plan.

mira_support: ACME says backfills started and then failed mid-run leaving mixed dims in index. They want remediation and a timeline — this is impacting search queries.

alex_eng: immediate mitigation options:
- temporarily accept both dims in indexer by padding/truncating vectors at read time (fast, risky for quality)
- re-embed all docs with the 1536->1024 conversion model (if possible) or full re-embed (expensive)
- reject heterogeneous batches and surface a clear error so customer can pause backfill and rerun with correct model

acme_ops: we need something that won't break live search. Padding would produce wrong results for high-precision queries. Full re-embed will take ~48 hours on their dataset (1.2M docs) but is safest.

jordan_sre: operationally, we can stage a canary re-embed for 10k docs to measure quality impact and time. Meanwhile, I can temporarily raise their per-minute quota + burst to let the backfill finish without hitting 429s. Need approval from billing first (risk of overage).

mira_support: action items: @alex_eng to provide a quick server-side guard that rejects mixed-dim batches with a more actionable error and link to docs; @jordan_sre to provision temporary quota bump + monitor; @ying_ml to help design canary re-embed and conversion plan; @acme_ops to pause backfill until we confirm approach. ETA: need customer-facing update in 90 minutes.

alex_eng: will put a small patch into indexer to change error message and add a diagnostic field with `model_used` per item. Patch diff (conceptual):
```diff
- raise VectorDimMismatch(req_id)
+ raise VectorDimMismatch(req_id, expected, got, sample_models=["open-embed-1536-v1","open-embed-1024-q4"])
```
This lets support surface which model produced which vector. I'll aim to deploy to staging in 45m and prod in 2h.

jordan_sre: bumped Acme per-minute quota from 480 -> 2000 for next 6 hours, monitoring metrics. Also increased embedding pool capacity by spinning up 2 extra slots in us-east-1. Watch dashboards for error rate and latency.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: alex_eng/indexer-dim-guard -> staging SUCCESS (build 1328).

acme_ops: tested paused backfill and ran a 1000-doc canary with the 1024 model — index accepted ~60% and rejected 40% (same mix). We confirmed some legacy cached embeddings were still 1536.

ying_ml: proposed canary plan:
- sample 10k docs across buckets (hot / cold / attachments)
- run both embed models and compare recall@10 against production queries
- measure time/cost for full rerun estimate
If canary shows minimal drop, proceed with full re-embed. If big drop, we should provide a conversion layer + notify devs.

mira_support: billing note — customer flagged concern: their spend spiked due to backfill and quota bump. Jordan — please get cost estimate so we can propose credit or pro-rate.

jordan_sre: estimated incremental infra cost for quota bump + extra slots ~ $320 for 6h. Full re-embed 1.2M docs at current throughput ~ $3.6k compute. I'll add numbers to the ticket.

alex_eng: follow-up deploy plan:
1) ship better diagnostic error to prod (2h).
2) once Acme pauses backfill, run canary (10k) with ying_ml (4h).
3) decide re-embed vs conversion (6h).
4) schedule full re-embed in maintenance window if agreed (48h run).

acme_ops: we paused the pipeline. Customer on call at 15:00 PDT to review canary. Thanks — please keep updates in this thread.

mira_support: summary for customer update (posting in ticket):
- root cause: model swap created mixed embedding dims because backfill continued with old cached embeddings.
- short-term: temporarily increased quota to avoid 429s and we updated indexer error messages to make the mismatch actionable.
- next steps: perform a 10k canary to measure quality and time. After canary, we will propose either a full re-embed or a conversion layer.
- ETA for canary results: ~6 hours.

acme_ops: ack, appreciate quick turnaround.

ying_ml: I'll start preparing canary datasets and scripts. Will post exact commands and seed ids here shortly.

mira_support: flagged as high priority. Escalating to Eng/ML/SRE. Will follow up with customer update in 60-90m.

ops-bot: ticket-bot: C-5492 updated: status=escalated, owner=mira_support, sla=P1

alex_eng: leaving a snippet of repro command (python) for the team:
```python
from redwood import EmbeddingsClient
client = EmbeddingsClient(api_key="<redacted>")
texts = ["doc1 text", "doc2 text", ...]
res = client.embed(texts, model="open-embed-1024-q4", batch_size=16)
# watch for responses with len != 1536
for i, r in enumerate(res):
    if len(r) != 1536:
        print(f"idx {i} got len {len(r)}")
```

mira_support: thanks all — I'll post the canary results and the customer-facing note once ying_ml and jordan_sre confirm.

acme_ops: leaving this thread, will wait for canary report.
